title: A lane lands the test-author's commits before the builder starts, and a builder never cherry-picks or amends a test commit
why: In #2536 the builder cherry-picked the test-author's commit and amended it, so it wrote a commit that held test files. The builder-diff guard was right to refuse. The fix is the lane's process, not the guard.
note: Likely false alarm, measured on #2536 (batch-local-checks-cmd), coordinator 07:12 CST Nov 10: the guard refused the builders' commits; the lane session committed the staged patches itself. Of the 7 commits, the 4 product commits touch only merge/merge.py and skills/ci-hygiene/SKILL.md; the 3 test commits touch only merge/test_lane_lint.py. The role split held. Lane's fix: judge only the builder's own commits. Red first: replay #2536's commit order. Related: builder-diff-merge-commit, builder-diff-auto-merge-reflog. Doing 07:13 CST Nov 10 in lane session_013NEJL3dPpqbux58j4atEY5 (coordinator). Rescoped 07:32 CST Nov 10 (coordinator): it was not a false alarm. The files held the role split, but the builder committed the test files itself. Lane-process fix, no guard change: a template change, built by lane session_013NEJL3dPpqbux58j4atEY5. Slug kept (steps are never renamed). Released to batch 72 as #2538 at 08:14 CST Nov 10 (coordinator): a template rule only, no guard change. The guard fix was refused, because cherry-pick -n then commit -C copies the trailer. A scratch repo proved main's guard right: it counts a builder's amend of a cherry-picked test commit as the builder's own. Any repo that copies the project-ops brief template picks it up.
